title: Native games, applications and eight-bit remake discovery
summary: Review 32 pinned roots: add 21 projects and record 11 evidence-qualified deferrals.
notes: Root personally performed 26 repository search queries across C64, ZX Spectrum, Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS/Windows. Deduplicated against current main containing 5407 projects and its source/decision indexes. Reviewed 32 pinned repository trees, their primary documentation and selected implementation files: 21 additions and 11 deferrals. Two further candidates were unavailable through the connector and are not promoted. Searches on Atari ST and CPC did not establish a new qualifying untracked addition; no platform quota was filled with irrelevant projects. Distinguish original CPU/platform from host target, redesigned remakes from matching source recovery, partial native engines from complete games, and game script interpreters from guest-CPU emulation. Preserve private build dependencies, original-data requirements and platform-test omissions. All build and equivalence claims remain author-attributed; no candidate code, installers, emulators or security-bypass instructions were executed. Selected file contents were fetched at pinned commits and exact blob hashes checked; larger files were inspected selectively and linked rather than embedded. Public submission omits source bodies. No discovery worker, branch or PR used.

sources.reason: Modern 3D remake with implemented combat state, weapon handling, animation and inventory systems. This is a redesigned revival of the C64 title, not recovered 6510 source or a matching reconstruction.

Recreates the 1985 C64 life simulation through native Godot state: money, food, drink, rest, appearance, education, NPCs and locations. Graphics and sound are remastered rather than original-binary reconstruction.

Implements tile collision, conveyors, falling, enemies and original-named levels in JavaScript. Author explicitly identifies differences in levels 19 and 20, title screen and unlock system; do not mark exact original parity.
Preserves Richard Phipps' Chaos: Battle of the Wizards remake. Semantic board, wizard and spell implementations use configurable spell lists and a WinMain game loop rather than Z80 emulation.

Godot remake of the John Heap/Paul Clancey Alien game: Nostromo rooms, crew movement and health, alien encounters, Jones, airlocks and self-destruct. README lists omissions while inspected code contains partial morale handling; complete parity is not established.

Reconstructs Splat's scrolling-border collection game as a one-to-four-player adaptation. Source implements original-lives and additional last-standing/infinite-lives scoring modes; multiplayer changes are not original-game equivalence.
Recreates rocket assembly, fuel collection, wrapping playfield and enemies as a four-player competitive adaptation. ShipConstruction implements separate assembly/fuel stages; not a matching Z80 port.
Recreates Deathchase as a Godot 3D/VR game with enemy bikers, pursuit distances, rockets and scenery. Scene and enemy logic are native GDScript rather than Spectrum CPU emulation.

Repository preserves an earlier C++/Allegro Styx remake under original/ and an unfinished Godot adaptation with spider spawning and level scenes. Level-editor documentation records gate and enemy behavior.
Native reconstruction of the 1997 Spectrum strategy game with unit combat tables, turn processing, cities, movement, fog and saves. It is a remake, not disassembled original source.

C99 reconstruction from WACKI.EXE with typed actor movement, waypoint routing, original asset decoding and a game-script VM. Script bytecode is a game subsystem, not an emulated host CPU. Author reports complete playthrough; this review does not independently certify it.

Reconstructs the Windows 3.1 Screen Antics screensaver in Rust, including TTM scene states, script semantics, resources, island behavior and rendering. Original resource/script interpreter is not x86 emulation.

Reconstructs the 1991 RPG through named C game routines and MASM video/intro modules. Original Microsoft C 5.1 small-model DGROUP layout is retained; source ties party/map structures to executable offsets.

Ports WINMINE.EXE procedures to JavaScript: board-byte layout, mine placement, flood-fill queue, first-click relocation, chording, timer and cheats. Address-linked notes and resource extraction distinguish this from a generic Minesweeper clone.

Function-by-function reconstruction of JPOG/Toshi with original exported names and ABI, kernel/property parser and game classes. README reports 9.1 percent reimplemented at review; hybrid x86 launch still depends on original DLLs, while portable standalone completion remains future work.

RE-derived remake of the 1989 Amiga game with original object-script disassembler, ADF/data extraction and classic-rule tests for hostages, shared search spots, cards and movement. Optional modern rules and 2.5D prototype are separate from original fidelity.

Semantic C++ translation of Magic Carpet and Hidden Worlds: named Thing/player structures, castle states, terrain, simulation and rendering linked to executable addresses. Author reports tick/pixel comparisons; no independent confirmation of whole-campaign or multiplayer parity.

Reconstructed DX-Ball game with semantic ball/brick/bonus rules and original PCX/SBK/BDS asset decoders. Port replaces Windows presentation/audio with SDL2 and FluidSynth; author reports 50 boards and 19 bonuses.

Recreates Dangerous Dave using native tile collision, player movement, enemies, bullets and audio. Source explicitly discusses original wall-climbing behavior; look-and-feel goal does not establish exact original logic.

RE-informed Go/Ebiten recreation with traditional Chinese interface, original-data parsing, combat and audit tools. Reported ending walkthrough used locked HP/one-hit cheats on both sides; not an independent ordinary-play completion test.

Reconstructs Softworld's 1991 Chinese strategy game and enhanced edition with original scenario/save formats and address-linked battle rules. Modern HD art, translations and expanded roster are remake extensions rather than original parity.

Fork of the already tracked dabadab Wizard of Wor disassembly. Extensive inherited 64tass source exists, but inspected evidence does not establish a sufficiently independent reconstruction to add another root.

Author explicitly replaces the original levels with newly designed inspired locations and uses newly sourced assets. Native combat code exists, but this is held as a fan-inspired new game rather than original-game reconstruction.
Source-backed LibGDX multiplayer remake of the ZX81 title, not a ZX Spectrum source game. Retain for a ZX81 pass rather than mislabel its original platform in this focused batch.

Inspected README describes the SGDK Sonic starter and source/pipeline does not establish completed Xeno reconstruction. Repository title alone is insufficient; hold for fuller implementation evidence.

Single large raw decompiler-output C file with undefined types and no build recipe or identified historical Notepad version. Useful lead, but not enough to classify as a usable retro application reconstruction.

NT4 screensaver research is described, but the repository consists chiefly of an IDA database and Cheat Engine table. The binary analysis database was not executed or decoded; defer until inspectable implementation or substantive text research can be reviewed.

Substantive 8086/NEC DSP speech-synthesizer firmware recovery, but original target is a hardware board rather than the requested DOS/Windows application platforms. Retain for a firmware-focused pass; do not relabel Windows host support as original Windows provenance.

Public decompilation research coexists with a playable path explicitly executing retail XANTH.EXE in its own 16-bit CPU/DOS runtime. README states no reimplemented game logic on that path. Keep for baked-emulation audit, not a native gameplay-reconstruction addition; reported 122/1000 route is incomplete.

Stars! 2.6i reconstruction infrastructure includes Win16 segmented-memory and API shims and a differential harness, but no substantive reconstructed game source directory is present in the reviewed tree. Defer until the actual game-function implementation and execution path can be evaluated.

Mixed native structured-C overrides and machine-state lifting: dec_rt pushes arguments onto an emulated stack and runtime/interp provides 8086 fallback and loaded sound-driver execution. Valuable partial decompilation, but runtime remains baked-emulation/mixed; hold for explicit execution-path audit rather than promote as fully native.

README describes instruction-derived remake and many features, but the pinned tree exposes manuals/configuration rather than maintainable implementation source. No release executable run; defer until source supports the reconstruction claim.
